stem: A Massachusetts patient presents a Schedule II oxycodone prescription written by her Massachusetts physician nine days earlier. She asks the pharmacy to dispense only part of it today and to hold the balance. A colleague says the initial partial fill is already too late because it is past the fifth day after the issue date. Which assessment is correct?

choices.text: The colleague is right; the five-day limit runs from the issue date for any Schedule II partial fill.
The colleague is right, but only because the drug is a narcotic rather than a stimulant.
The colleague is wrong; the five-day limit reaches only prescriptions filled on the out-of-state pathways.
The colleague is wrong; no deadline governs a patient-requested partial fill of a Schedule II prescription.
The colleague is wrong; the five-day limit runs from the first dispensing rather than from the issue date.

explanation.core_reasoning: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(d3/4) contains two deadlines with different reach. The remaining portion must be filled not later than 30 days after the prescription issue date. The five-day limit on the initial partial dispensing applies only to a prescription filled pursuant to subsection (d) or (d1/2) -- respectively a nonnarcotic Schedule II prescription issued by an out-of-state practitioner, and a narcotic Schedule II prescription issued by a practitioner registered in Maine or a contiguous state. This prescription came from a Massachusetts physician, so neither pathway is engaged and the initial partial fill on day nine is in time.

choice_analysis.A: The five-day limit is conditioned on the prescription having been filled under s. 18(d) or (d1/2).
choice_analysis.B: The narcotic distinction separates (d) from (d1/2); both remain out-of-state pathways.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: subsections (d) and (d1/2) are the out-of-state prescriber pathways.
choice_analysis.D: The 30-day remainder deadline still governs, measured from the issue date.
choice_analysis.E: Both deadlines in the subsection are measured from the prescription issue date.

related_facts: Only the pharmacy that dispensed the lesser quantity may dispense the remaining portion
explanation.mpje_trap: The five-day figure is real and sits in the same subsection, which makes it easy to apply to a prescription the subsection never sends down that path.

reasoning_steps: Identify where the prescription was issued and under which subsection it is filled
Match each deadline in s. 18(d3/4) to the pathway it governs
Measure the surviving deadline from the prescription issue date
